name: rotor-bob
note: Vertical demand at hover, mirrored: +25 deg then -25 deg about a level datum, so climb and descent are equal-magnitude steps. NOT QUEUED FOR THE 2026-08-02 NIGHT RUN, and read R39-rotor 4 before scheduling it: THIS CARD CANNOT COMMAND A VERTICAL MANEUVER. The mod writes an aim direction and a throttle pin and never touches collective, so 'bobdn' is a nose-down POINTING step - it produced +1.0 m/s (AttackHelo1) and +0.5 m/s (QuadVTOL1), both still CLIMBING during the segment. A genuine descent test is worth having now that the game's VRS envelope is known exactly (engages above 4 + 0.4 x in-plane airspeed m/s of descent through the disk), but it needs a card that can pin a LOW collective, and no card can: ScenarioPlayer.OwnInputs returns early at EntrySpeed <= 0, so a declared hover flies at the level-hold's TestDrone.HoldThrottle = 0.60 and a config pin on Scenario/ScenarioThrottle is read after the early return. Its pass/fail signal would be the descent rate against that VRS threshold, not anything the control law does. ENTRY IS A REAL HOVER, same as rotor-hover: startSpeed 0 is DECLARED, so since v1.0.0 the aircraft is placed at 0 m/s at startAlt with a controller reset per replicate. Pre-v1.0.0 captures of this card were flown in forward flight (debugtests/R39-rotor.md) and are not comparable. startAlt raised 1000 -> 2500 m: at the Drone/DroneAltDeckM 3000 default, 1000 put the LOWER deck at -500 m MSL, under the 500 m card floor, so half the fleet aborted on its first tick. 2500 keeps both decks (1000 / 4000 m) above the floor if the knob is forgotten - set it to 0 anyway, or one of the three airframes flies at a different air density from the other two. The airframe list names the three rotorcraft outright, for the same reason rotor-hover does - an empty list fell through to Drone/DroneAirframe and cls then refused the card on every lane. A tiltwing/VTOL must already be in the HOVER configuration (a card never writes customAxis1).
